merger_description:
Eldridge Ausenco MidCo 3, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of Eldridge Industries, LLC (**Eldridge**), proposes to acquire 100% of the shares in Ausenco Pty Ltd (**Ausenco**) from Resource Capital Fund VI L.P and 18 minority shareholders.

Eldridge is an investment holding company with a diversified portfolio, managing businesses and investing in various industries such as asset management, insurance, technology, sports and gaming and real estate. Headquartered in New York, Eldridge Industries has offices in Greenwich, London, and Beverly Hills with over 3,000 employees.

Ausenco is an engineering, construction, consulting, and project delivery company, providing solutions for large-scale industrial and urban infrastructure projects.

Headquartered in Brisbane, Australia, Ausenco has 21 offices in 9 countries, with projects taking place in over 100 locations worldwide. The company serves customers globally through locations including in Canada, the United States, Chile, Mexico, Australia, Brazil, and Argentina.

Ausenco’s service offering includes consulting services, project delivery, operations and maintenance, and sustainability solutions to businesses operating in three primary industry sectors:

* Minerals and Metals: Ausenco offers environmental consulting services on a diverse range of mine designs and project management and development, from exploration and conceptual stages to feasibility studies. Support of customers’ mining projects include exploration geology, resources geology, geotechnical geology and tunnelling engineering. Ausenco has experience with a variety of commodities including precious and base metals, copper and gold.
* Oil and Gas: Ausenco offers oil and gas clients a variety of services that handle a range of oil and gas commodities, including gas, LPG/LNG and oil sands. These services include upstream consulting, arctic engineering, marine terminal and logistics studies and geotechnical engineering.
* Industrial and Infrastructure: Ausenco has experience with developing solutions for largescale infrastructure projects in both public and private sectors. These projects include bridges, roads and light rail to water, sewer, and wastewater treatment systems. Ausenco provides a range of consulting, engineering and project delivery services in industrial commodities including biomass, industrial chemicals, and plastics.

determination_table_content.details:
Eldridge Ausenco MidCo 3, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of
Eldridge Industries, LLC (Eldridge), applied for a notification waiver in
respect of its proposed acquisition of 100% of the share capital in
Ausenco Pty Ltd (Ausenco), as described in the transaction
documents provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Eldridge, is an investment holding company with a
diversified portfolio, managing businesses and investing in various
industries such as asset management, insurance, technology, sports
and gaming and real estate. Headquartered in New York, Eldridge
Industries has offices in Greenwich, London, and Beverly Hills with
over 3,000 employees.
The target, Ausenco, is an engineering, construction, consulting, and
project delivery company, providing solutions for large-scale
industrial and urban infrastructure projects.
Headquartered in Brisbane, Australia, Ausenco has 21 offices in 9
countries, with projects taking place in over 100 locations worldwide.
The company serves customers globally through locations in
Canada, the United States, Chile, Mexico, Australia, Brazil, and
Argentina among others.
Ausenco’s service offering includes consulting services, project
delivery, operations and maintenance, and sustainability solutions to
businesses operating in three primary industry sectors: minerals and
metals; oil and gas; and industrial and infrastructure.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given there is no horizontal overlap or
vertical relationship between Eldridge (or its connected entities) and
Ausenco in the supply of engineering and consulting services in
Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
